extracted.intended_audience: NIH K99/R00 review committee; K99 applicants and mentors (advisory committee members)
extracted.subtask_description: Mentor, co-mentor, and collaborator letters and institutional statements describing commitments, training plans, resources, and timelines provided to a K99/R00 candidate to support research, career development, and transition to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate writing independence and productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: I allow Ryo to independently write his manuscripts and grants, and the first draft presented to me is always a fully completed document. To hone his writing skills further, we work together on improving manuscripts, and we work both electronically and in person as I go over how to strengthen his work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of independent drafting of manuscripts and grants, plus mentor involvement to improve writing; documented publication record (e.g., 7 first-author manuscripts in Liza’s lab; two manuscripts in mentor's lab; involvement in high-impact submissions such as Nature and Cell) strengthens the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular advisory/committee meeting schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: During the K99 phase of the grant, Ryo will meet with the advisory committee every 6 months to discuss research progress. In my capacity as a co-mentor, Ryo and I will have monthly meetings..., Ryo and I have agreed to meet every three months with more frequent meetings when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify frequencies (e.g., monthly, every 3 months, every 6 months), note that meetings should be more frequent during intensive experimental phases; commitments from mentors to participate are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined transition-to-independence plan
rubrics_metrics.description: At the culmination of Year 1, we will assess whether Ryo is prepared to step into the faculty search process. I fully expect that Ryo will have an impressive CV and necessary skillsets to successfully begin his faculty search at the beginning of Year 2. I will work with Ryo through the application, interview, and negotiation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear milestone-based plan (assessment at end of Year 1, start faculty search Year 2) and mentor support for applications, interviews, and negotiations are expected components of a K99 mentorship plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities for presentations and networking
rubrics_metrics.description: I will encourage Ryo to give talks at several conferences and seminars during the K99 phase...plans to present at Keystone Symposia, Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Meetings, Gordon Research Conferences, and in several bay area meetings... send Ryo to the Molecular and Cell Biology and Genetics departmental retreats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor should identify concrete meeting and seminar opportunities that will broaden the candidate's visibility and networks; frequency and targeted conferences strengthen the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on technical training in proposed methods
rubrics_metrics.description: My lab is highly experienced and well equipped to perform ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, and RNAseq in C. elegans, and my lab members will train him to become proficient in both the technical work and post-sequencing analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor/collaborator must state specific techniques they will train the candidate on and indicate lab personnel who will provide that training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bioinformatics and computational training commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Currently, all members of my lab have been individually trained to perform their own bioinformatics analyses, using various different software, including bowtie2, SAMtools, deepTools, and macs2 for ATAC-seq and CHIP-seq, and tophat and cufflinks for RNAseq. During his training, I will have Ryo attend the python and R bootcamps taught at UC Berkeley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific software/tools and available courses (e.g., python and R bootcamps); explicit plans for computational skill acquisition and independence (e.g., independence within first year) are desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined timeline and milestones for skill acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: I fully expect Ryo to be independent in post-sequence analyses within his first year in my lab. After this initial year of training, my lab and I will continue to provide feedback and support throughout the K99 portion of the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete timelines (e.g., independence in analyses by year 1) and post-training support; milestones help reviewers assess feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active in-lab mentoring and feedback mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: This will be in the form of direct in-lab mentoring, as well as experimental and scientific feedback during lab meetings, which Ryo will attend and present regularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe routine feedback venues (lab meetings, one-on-one mentoring, group presentations) and expectations for candidate participation/presentation frequency (e.g., present regularly, at least every 6 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor track record of trainee success
rubrics_metrics.description: I have extensive experience in mentoring Ph.D. students and post-doctoral fellows...Of my 38 Ph.D. students and 37 postdoctoral fellows, virtually all have prominent positions as faculty, senior scientists in industry, or scientific writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide mentor's historical outcomes for trainees to demonstrate successful mentorship and likely positive career outcomes for the candidate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor/collaborator commitments spelled out in letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: I write with enthusiastic support...and commitment to serve both as a mentor on Ryo Higuchi-Sanabria’s advisory committee, and a collaborator...Ryo and I have agreed to meet at least twice a year, with more frequent meetings during times when he will be working on developing his ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq platforms in his lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should specifically state the nature of the commitment (mentorship, collaboration), frequency of meetings, types of support (training, data analysis, protocol development), and names of personnel involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to institutional core facilities and technical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The UC Davis Genome Center...we can perform all of Rye's mass-spec work and the bioinformatics core can assist...we have Thermo Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer...two medium-sized computer clusters and one large 400 core cluster that we can access for data analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify core facilities, instrumentation, and computational resources that will be available to the candidate and describe staff expertise to support experiments and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative method development and validation support
rubrics_metrics.description: We are designing and now optimizing the use a sequence of immunoblots...to distinguish between G-actin and F-actin species...we are adapting a serial lysis technique...our preliminary work gives us full confidence that we can optimize this technique towards the analysis of actin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborators should describe concrete method-development roles, timelines for optimization and validation, and expected outputs (e.g., manuscript submissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of professional development (teaching, course participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: I will continue to increase my teaching skills by participating in running his laboratory course, and will design and run the lab course in subsequent semesters. Outside of the lab, Drs. Dillin and Meyer participate in many leading conferences and meetings around the world, which he invites senior members of his lab to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify opportunities for the candidate to gain teaching experience and to participate in educational activities that support the development of an independent faculty profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance with job negotiation, staff hiring, and lab management
rubrics_metrics.description: During the R00 phase, I will assist Ryo in any way I can...My lab manager, Larry Joe, will aid in his equipment negotiation and interviewing prospective hires as he builds his lab...I will also push for Ryo to give talks in meetings I organize, and help in staff acquisition by forwarding candidates that I believe will be a great fit in his lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor commitments to provide practical support for starting a lab (equipment negotiation, interviewing hires, identifying candidates) and ongoing career support during R00 strengthen the transition plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement and opportunities to mentor others
rubrics_metrics.description: I continue to encourage Ryo to work with both graduate students and postdocs in their writing so that he can acquire mentorship skills and learn various writing styles. I will introduce him to postdocs and graduate students in my lab to aid in his mentorship and growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide structured opportunities for the candidate to mentor junior trainees (co-supervision, training roles) to build leadership and mentoring experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional environment quality and networking advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: UC Berkeley is a well-established and leading research institute across the country...the university currently employs 21 MacArthur fellows, 7 Nobel laureates, and 144 members of the National Academy of Sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe institutional strengths (prestige, faculty caliber, seminars and retreats) and how they provide networking, visibility, and additional mentorship opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to candidate productivity and publication support
rubrics_metrics.description: I will assist Ryo...for feedback on grant applications, papers, scientific direction...He has already published a very thorough review and primary literature article...He also has two first-author articles coming up shortly: one currently under review in Cell...and another under revision for Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors should commit to helping refine manuscripts and grants and list existing/forthcoming publications as evidence of productivity and feasibility of the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of named personnel to provide technical mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: In my lab, he will work directly with Drs. Erika Anderson, Nick Fuda, and Kristina Krassovsky, who regularly perform the types of experiments laid out in his proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specific lab members who will train the candidate and their relevant expertise to demonstrate hands-on support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of presentation in mentor's group for feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Ryo will present regularly (at least every 6 months) during my lab’s group meeting to get directed feedback from all members of my lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify minimum presentation frequency within mentor's group meetings to ensure regular critical feedback and integration into the mentor's research community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit collaborative endorsements with expected deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: If all goes accordingly to plan, I estimate our first manuscript submission this calendar year...we are designing and now optimizing...we have reported on successful immunoblotting...our preliminary work gives us full confidence that we can optimize this technique towards the analysis of actin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should include milestones or deliverables (e.g., expected manuscript submission) tied to the collaboration to demonstrate feasibility and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated candidate qualities: work ethic, teamwork, and lab citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: It is clear through Ryo's exceptional and diverse CV that he is an excellent scientist with extraordinary work ethic...He also goes above and beyond to ensure that the lab runs smoothly, being the first to volunteer in making reagents, cleaning, dealing with trash and hazardous resources, ordering, or anything that could possibly help in any way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor narratives that emphasize interpersonal skills, teamwork, and lab citizenship provide evidence the candidate will be an effective leader and colleague.
